name: print what chance alone scores, under the result
one_line: The number saying what somebody who understood nothing would have got, worked out in advance and printed under the blank, never above it.
how: For anything with a countable outcome, work out what random play gets, and print that number under the place where the person writes their own. Jumping coins at random finishes with one left 0.69% of the time and with four nearly half the time. Firing at random on a seven-by-seven grid takes 46 shots against about 33 played well. Playing Kuhn poker as well as it can be played still loses a bean in eighteen hands. It is not the answer and cannot be copied into the blank; it is the floor. Below, it says a poor result was expected. Above, it is a target read before anything is attempted, and the sheet has answered itself.

knobs.effect: Chance alone gives a floor and makes a poor result the expected one without a word of consolation. The best possible gives a ceiling. A measured fact about what other people did gives neither and is often the most interesting of the three.
Below, it is a term of comparison for something already written. Above, it is a target, and everything written afterwards has been leaned on by it.
Computed exactly, it can be printed as it stands and defended. Estimated and printed as a figure it will be read as measured, and an invented floor is worse than no floor at all.
Random coin-jumping stops at four almost half the time, so nearly finishing is mostly luck. Wherever the distribution of chance is lumpy, how close somebody got carries no information about them.

where_the_work_is: In the number being calculated instead of felt. A guessed floor is decoration; a computed one is the only thing that makes «I finished with four» mean anything to whoever reads the sheet afterwards.
breaks: It adds nothing that comes back beyond a number already printed, so it is never the point of a moment. The calculation is real work, usually a few lines of code, and it has to be done before anything goes to the printer. On a display one number and the thing it is a floor for both fit, and the working does not — but a floor separated from its subject means nothing, so a display can only ever carry the pair.
